The '''2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' (SHC) was the 134th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier [[inter-county]] [[hurling]] tournament, since its establishment in [[1887 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1887]]. The competition began on 26 June and ended on 22 August 2021.

[[Antrim county hurling team|Antrim]], having won the [[2020 Joe McDonagh Cup]], returned to the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] for the first time since the [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|2015 competition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189899.html|title=Antrim see off Kerry to secure McDonagh Cup success at Croke Park |date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=13 December 2020|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2020/1213/1184237-cusack-fears-for-antrim-in-2021-leinster-championship/|title=Cusack fears for Antrim in 2021 Leinster championship|work=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=13 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref> [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] entered the competition as the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Superb Limerick regain All-Ireland title with emphatic win|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 December 2020|access-date=13 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref>

The [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|final]] was played on 22 August 2021 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between Limerick and [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]], in what was their first ever meeting in a final. Limerick won the match with a display that is regarded by many to be one of the greatest performances by a team in an All-Ireland Final. Limerick showed immense dominance in the first half opening a 13-point gap, the scores 3–18 to 1–11 at the interval. This dominance would continue in the second half in more subdued fashion but Limerick still managed to extend their lead to 16 by the final whistle, the full time score 3–32 to 1–22. This was the first time that Limerick won consecutive editions of this competition, the team's an overall tenth tenth title, as well as a third title in four seasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242236-limerick-crush-cork-to-claim-back-to-back-all-irelands/|title=Limerick crush Cork to claim back-to-back All-Irelands|work=[[RTÉ Sport]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}</ref>

Cork's [[Patrick Horgan]] was the championship's top scorer with 0–54.

Limerick captain [[Declan Hannon]] became only the second captain after [[Christy Ring]] to lift the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] on three occasions.

==Format change==

In December 2020, a plan by the Central Competitions Control Committee (CCCC) was approved by the GAA's management committee. The plan saw the re-introduction of the provincial knock-out/qualifier system, in line with the pre-2018 format, thus resulting in the provincial round robins being temporarily discarded.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/no-super-8s-or-hurling-round-robin-new-league-format-and-county-before-club-gaa-approve-plan-for-2021-season-39879571.html|title=No Super 8s or hurling round robin, new league format and county before club – GAA approve plan for 2021 season|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> Relegation to and promotion from the [[Joe McDonagh Cup]] was re-introduced. The two beaten Leinster quarter-final teams are due to play a preliminary qualifier round, with the losers dropping to the McDonagh Cup and winners progressing to round 1 of the qualifiers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-revamped-2021-season-calendar-5280615-Dec2020/|title=GAA set to unveil plan for 2021 season with inter-county February start and July All-Ireland finals|publisher=The 42|date=21 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}}</ref>

Round 1 of the qualifiers will feature the playoff winners playing a Munster quarter-finalist or semi-finalist, and a Leinster semi-finalist playing a Munster quarter-finalist or semi-finalist.

Round 2 of the qualifiers will feature the Round 1 winners playing a Munster or Leinster semi-finalist, with the winners advancing to the All-Ireland quarter-finals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.meathchronicle.ie/2021/06/04/all-the-football-and-hurling-championship-fixtures-and-dates/|title=All the football and hurling championship fixtures and dates|website=Meath Chronicle}}</ref>

The draws for the hurling championship were delayed until 19 and 20 April 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/munster-shc-draw-5413834-Apr2021/|title=Limerick and Cork set for Munster SHC semi-final showdown|date=19 April 2021|work=The 42|accessdate= 20 April 2021}}</ref>

==Miscellaneous==

*Limerick won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] three-in-a-row for the first time since [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1934]]–[[1935 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1935]]–[[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1936]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/650126/85-year-wait-ends-as-limerick-topple-tipperary-to-win-historic-munster-hurling-title.html#:~:text=and%20improve%20products.-,85%2Dyear%20wait%20ends%20as%20Limerick%20topple%20Tipperary,win%20historic%20Munster%20hurling%20title&text=The%20final%20score%20in%20Pairc,the%20province%20between%201933%2D36.|title=85-year wait ends as Limerick topple Tipperary to win historic Munster hurling title|date=18 July 2021|work=Limerick Leader|accessdate= 24 July 2021}}</ref>
*Kilkenny's sixth year in a row without an All-Ireland senior title, equalling their title drought of 1994–1999.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.corkbeo.ie/sport/gaa/cork-v-kilkenny-ireland-senior-21250548|title=Cork v Kilkenny All-Ireland Senior Hurling Semi-Final Full Preview|first=James|last=Clancy|date=August 7, 2021|website=Cork Beo}}</ref>
*Cork's sixteenth year in a row without an All-Ireland senior title, surpassing their title drought of 1904–1918.
*It was the first ever All-Ireland final between Cork and Limerick.
*It was the first Munster final between Limerick and Tipperary since 2019.
*It was the first Leinster final between Dublin and Kilkenny since 2014.
*It was the first Joe McDonagh Cup final between Antrim and Kerry since 2020.
*Limerick scored 3–32 (41 points) in the All-Ireland final, the highest ever score in a final.
*It is the first time since Kilkenny in 2014–2015 that a county team won back-to-back All Ireland Hurling Championship titles. 
*Limerick retained the All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship for the first time in their history. This was their tenth title, making them the first county outside the [[Big Three (hurling)|Big Three]] to reach double figures.
*Limerick became the 6th county in history to win back-to-back All-Ireland hurling titles after Kilkenny, Cork, Tipperary, Galway and Wexford.
*Cork reached the final for the first time since [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]].
*Two new [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship records and statistics|scoring feats]] were achieved on 24 July. [[Joe Canning]] surpassed [[Henry Shefflin]]'s record haul to become the all-time top championship scorer.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://hoganstand.com/Galway/article/index/318774|title=Canning breaks all-time scoring record but can't prevent Galway's defeat to Deise|date=24 July 2021|work=Hogan Stand|accessdate= 24 July 2021}}</ref> [[Patrick Horgan]] became the third player, after Canning and Shefflin, to have broken the 500-point barrier.
*Limerick played against Tipperary, Waterford and Cork twice (Munster Semi-final and All-Ireland Final) to retain the Liam MacCarthy cup, the first time — and only time, to date — that any county won a championship playing only teams from a single province, in this case all Munster opposition.
*Limerick had eleven players represented on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' team of the year, a first for any male intercounty team in both Hurling and Gaelic Football, beating the previous record of nine representatives held by both Limerick in 2020 and Kilkenny in 2008.
